chunks: More than one of our companions told me, from Muhammad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Kufi, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, who said: We were told by al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan, who said: We were told by Bakr, from al-Qasim ibn Urwa, from al-Abd al-Hamid al-Ta'i, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)
about the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He: «And I blew into him from My Spirit». How was this blowing?

So he said: Indeed, the Spirit is moving like the wind, and it was only named a Spirit because its name was derived from wind, and He only extracted it on the phrase of Spirit because a spirit is homogenic to wind, and He only added it to Himself because He selected it over other spirits, like how He has selected one house among the houses and said: My House, and how He said to a Messenger among the Messengers: My Good Friend, and the likes of so.
All of that is created, made, subject to a Lord and is managed.
ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'My Spirit' in the context of Adam's creation according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates the phrase 'I blew into him from My Spirit' by identifying the 'Spirit' as a created, moving entity akin to wind, derived linguistically from the word for wind. He explains that attributing it to God is a matter of selection and honor, similar to calling a house 'My House' or a prophet 'My Friend', and emphasizes that this Spirit is a created, manufactured, and governed entity.

en.basel-kadem: 12.	I was told by more than one of our companions, from Muhammed bin Abi Abdillah al-Kufi, from Muhammed bin Isma’il, that he said: We were told by Hussain bin Hasan, that he said: We were told by Bikr, from Qasim bin Urwa, from Abdul-Hameed al-Ta’I, from Muhammed bin Muslim, that he said: I asked Abu Ja’far, peace be upon him,
about the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He: «And I blew into him from My Spirit» [15:29]. How was this blowing?

So he said: «Indeed, the Spirit is moving like the wind, and it was only named a Spirit [1] because its name was derived from wind [2], and He only extracted it on the phrase of Spirit because a spirit is homogenic to wind, and He only added it to Himself because He selected it over other spirits, like how He has selected one house among the houses and said: My House, and how He said to a Messenger among the Messengers: My Good Friend, and the likes of so.
All of that is created, made, subject to a Lord and is managed.
